note: THE JOIN TABLE. A THEME binds the 4 independent vectors: Color, Typography, Forms, and Spacing. Apps reference a THEME slug via THEMES.applyTheme(slug) and the resolver composes all four. schemaVersion 3 (2026-07-19): confirmed 4-pointer shape end-to-end + added composed utility themes now that resolve.js actually applies every vector.

vocabulary.color: entity — the palette (hue only). e.g. maw-dark-utility.
vocabulary.typography: entity — fonts + size ramp + tracking. e.g. sharp-racing.
vocabulary.forms: entity — tactility: radii, border weight, shadows, elevation, motion, gradient angle. sharp | soft | grounded.
vocabulary.spacing: entity — density: touch target, padding, gaps. tight | standard | loose | flush | database.
vocabulary.theme: JOIN — named combination of exactly one token from each of the four vectors.

themes.name: Sharp Utility
themes.intendedUse: Tight instrument/data look — the sleek dashboard direction (Retrocast).

themes.name: Soft Utility
themes.intendedUse: Balanced everyday default for new apps copied from template-app.

themes.name: Soft Racing · Mercedes
themes.intendedUse: soft-utility's feel with the Mercedes palette — petronas teal accent on a near-black green-tinted ground, silver as the secondary. Built 2026-07-30 for inciardi-collection. A pure COLOR swap: typography/forms/spacing are byte-identical to soft-utility, so anything that reads correctly in one reads correctly in the other.

themes.name: Sharp Carbon
themes.intendedUse: Neutral-cool tight instrument look; alternative to sharp-utility.

themes.name: Database
themes.intendedUse: THE DATABASE LOOK (Michael, 2026-08-03) — maximum row density, gaps collapsed, chrome out of the way. Named for the words he actually uses, so 'give me the database look' resolves in a grep, in this file and in the spacing grid. Deliberately `sharp-utility` with ONE pointer changed (spacing tight -> database) so the two are comparable and any difference is attributable to spacing alone. ⚠️ status DRAFT: composed but never rendered — nothing has consumed it yet, so nobody has looked at it. Promote to locked only after it has been seen. ⚠️ SIBLING, NOT A RIVAL: the `flush` spacing row is the other dense option and it optimises a DIFFERENT axis — flush hugs the viewport EDGE, database maximises ROWS. If nobody can state that difference on sight, retire one rather than letting both drift.

themes.name: On Track · Racing Bulls
themes.intendedUse: The On Track motorsport schedule — navy+red Racing Bulls identity, Archivo display headers, rounded soft chrome. Series identity colors ride on top as a local layer (not theme tokens). ⚠️ 2026-08-01: the `red-bull` COLOR row's accent moved from red to the can's yellow (the board rework — four teams were sharing one red). This theme's chrome accent therefore changed with it. If On Track wants the old red it is now `accent-2` on the same row, or it gets its own color entity — do NOT add a local override.

themes.name: Eos
themes.intendedUse: Lighting/theatrical apps — ETC Eos console grammar (tombstone display: magenta=tracked, blue=intensity-up, green=lower/marked, gold=captured/selected, red=manual). Shared across the LX-notes clone, the Eos Tombstone Teaching Tool, and future lighting tools.

themes.name: F1 Racetracks
themes.intendedUse: THE f1-racetracks app's single point of entry to the theme system (Michael, 2026-08-01). Named for the app on purpose: it is an app identity, not a constructor palette, and no team owns violet. Every pointer reproduces what the app already renders, so adopting it is a swap of a hand-baked layer for one pointer rather than a restyle — `sharp` forms are already copied verbatim into chrome-tokens.css section 7 (J20), `sharp-racing` is already the Chakra Petch / Inter / JetBrains Mono set the brand lockup hardcodes, `tight` matches a dense results board, and `paddock` is the app's own hue-268 ramp. ⚠️ Team colours are NOT in this join and must never be swept into one: a theme applies ONE AT A TIME, the standings matrix renders eleven teams AT ONCE (J14). They stay a local identity layer read from colors.tsv as data.

themes.name: Papyrus
themes.intendedUse: Warm editorial / HML LLC FileMaker renders and natural-light applications. Gabarito display, IBM Plex Mono, zero-radius base, subtle parchment shadows. Spacing uses tight (shared) — FMP density matches.
